Summarize the following for a technical audience in 5 bullet points, then list two open questions.

Mixture-of-experts language models route each token to a small subset of feed-forward experts selected by a learned gate. Because only a fraction of the parameters is active per token, compute per token is low, but the full set of experts must still be stored. On consumer hardware the experts are often kept in system memory and either computed on the CPU or copied to the GPU on demand. Routing statistics show strong skew: a minority of experts receives most of the traffic, and consecutive tokens often reuse experts. Caching hot experts on the GPU therefore captures a large share of the work, but the remaining misses cross the PCIe bus, whose bandwidth is one to two orders of magnitude below that of GPU memory. Prefetching based on the next layer's likely routing can hide part of the latency, while speculative decoding increases the number of distinct experts touched per forward pass.

```python
def f(a):
    s, best, lo = {}, 0, 0
    for hi, x in enumerate(a):
        if x in s and s[x] >= lo:
            lo = s[x] + 1
        s[x] = hi
        best = max(best, hi - lo + 1)
    return best
```
